--- SOURCE PAGE 12 ---
Poorvi—Grade 6

I lived first in a little house,
 And lived there very well,
 I thought the world was small and round,
 And made of pale, blue shell.

I lived next in a little nest,
 Nor needed any other,
 I thought the world was made of straw,
 And nestled by my mother.

One day, I fluttered from my nest,
 To see what I could find,
 I said the world is made of leaves,
 I have been very blind.

At length I flew beyond the tree,
 Quite fit for grown-up labours,
 I don’t know how the world is made,
 And neither do my neighbours.

The Bird's First Perception of the World

According to the text, the baby bird thought its first world was small, round, and light blue. It was made of a pale, blue shell and nestled by its mother.

The Bird's Second Perception of the World

After leaving the shell, the bird saw leaves and thought it had been very blind. It felt the world was warm and comfortable, made of straw, with its mother nearby.

The Bird's Final Perception of the World

At length, the bird flew beyond the tree and said the world is made of leaves. However, it also realized that it had been very blind because it could not see the leaves from its nest.

The Bird's Adult Perception of the World

When the bird became an adult, it flew away and said the world is made of leaves. It also realized that it had been very blind because it could not see the leaves from its nest.
